definitions.explanation: A double-edged sword or blade. While {刀|かたな} refers specifically to the single-edged Japanese sword, {剣|けん} is a broader term that can refer to swords in general, including Western-style double-edged swords and swords in fantasy/game contexts.

examples.japanese: {勇者|ゆうしゃ}が{剣|けん}を{抜|ぬ}いた。
{剣|けん}の{腕|うで}を{磨|みが}くために{毎日|まいにち}{稽古|けいこ}する。
examples.english: I practice every day to improve my swordsmanship.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}には{古代|こだい}の{剣|けん}や{鎧|よろい}が{数多|かずおお}く{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: Many ancient swords and suits of armor are on display at the museum.

notes:
Also read as つるぎ, which sounds more literary and archaic. The けん reading is standard in modern compounds and everyday use.

In Japanese martial arts, {剣|けん} often appears in compound words related to swordsmanship. In games and fantasy fiction, {剣|けん} is the standard word for swords of all types.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {剣|けん}を{抜|ぬ}く — to draw a sword
- {剣|けん}を{振|ふ}る — to swing a sword
- {剣道|けんどう} — kendo (Japanese fencing)
- {剣術|けんじゅつ} — swordsmanship
- {剣士|けんし} — swordsman, fencer
- {真剣|しんけん} — real sword; seriousness
